div.l: And whiche they were ⁊and of what degree
And eke in what aray þat they were inne
And at a knight þan I woll first begynne
A knyght þer was ⁊and þat a worthie man
That fro þe tyme þat he first began
To riden out . he loued chyualrye
Trouthe ⁊and honour fredom ⁊and curtesy
Full worthie was he in his lordes warre
⁊and there to hadde he ryden no man farre
As well in cristendom as in hethenesse
And euer honoured for his worthinesse
At alisaundre he was whan it wonne
Full ofte tyme / he hadde the bord bygonne
Aboue alle nations in Pruce
In lettowe had he reysed ⁊and in ruce
No crystene man so ofte of his degree
In gernade at þᵉ sege ek had he bee
Of algezure ⁊and riden in belmarye
At lycio was he ⁊and at satalye
When they were wonne ⁊and in þᵉ grete see
At many a noble armeye had he be
At morteill battailles had he bene fiftene
⁊and foughten for our faith at tramessene
In lystes thryes ⁊and ay slain his foo
This ilk worthie knight had bene also
Somtyme with the lord of Palatye
Ayeyn an other hethen in Turkye
And euermore he had a souereyne prys
And though þat he was worthie he was wys
And of his port as meke as is a mayde
He neuer yet no velonye ne saide
In all his lif vnto no manere wight
He was a very parfite gentill knyght
For to tellen yow of his armey
His hors weren gode ; but he was not gay
Of fustion he werede a gepon
All besmotered with his habirgeon
For he was late ycome from his viage
⁊and went for to done his pylgrymage
